title: Introduction to Tag Helpers
description: Understand what tag helpers are, how they simplify HTML generation, and how to enable them in your ASP.NET Core app.

data.text: Tag Helpers let server-side C# code participate in creating and rendering HTML elements. Instead of writing raw HTML strings in your views, you use attributes like `asp-controller` and `asp-action` on standard HTML elements. ASP.NET Core transforms those attributes into real HTML before the page reaches the browser.

Tag Helpers solve a common problem: HTML written by hand is verbose and fragile. If a route changes, you must update every hard-coded `href` or `action` attribute across many views. Tag Helpers generate those URLs for you, staying in sync with your routing configuration automatically.

terms.definition: An attribute or element that ASP.NET Core transforms into standard HTML during view rendering.
A tag helper shipped with ASP.NET Core, such as the Anchor, Form, or Input tag helpers.
A tag helper you write yourself by deriving from TagHelper to transform HTML in a domain-specific way.
A Razor file that centrally registers tag helpers so they are available in all views.

data.caption: How a Tag Helper transforms an HTML element
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Razor View (.cshtml)
    participant R as Razor Engine
    participant TH as Tag Helper
    participant B as Browser

    V->>R: a asp-controller="Home" asp-action="Index"
    R->>TH: Match element to TagHelper by attribute
    TH->>TH: Process(context, output)
    TH->>R: Set output.TagName, output.Attributes
    R->>B: a href="/Home/Index"

data.text: Before you can use built-in tag helpers, you must register them in `_ViewImports.cshtml`. This file lives in the `Views` folder and applies to every view in the project:

data.title: Views/_ViewImports.cshtml — enabling built-in tag helpers
data.content: Register all built-in MVC tag helpers for every view.

data.text: The first argument (`*`) means all tag helpers in the given assembly. The second argument is the assembly name. When you create custom tag helpers later, you will add a second line pointing to your own assembly.

data.title: Already there in MVC templates
data.text: Projects created with the ASP.NET Core Web App (Model-View-Controller) template include this line automatically. If you start from an Empty template, add it yourself.
ASP.NET Core ships with tag helpers for common tasks:

items: Anchor Tag Helper — builds `href` from controller, action, and route values.
Form Tag Helper — builds the `action` attribute and adds an antiforgery token.
Input, Label, Select, TextArea Tag Helpers — bind HTML form controls to model properties.
Cache Tag Helper — caches rendered content for a specified duration.
JavaScript and CSS Tag Helpers — manage script and stylesheet includes with CDN fallback support.

data.text: When built-in helpers are not enough, you can write custom tag helpers. A custom tag helper is a C# class that derives from `TagHelper` and overrides the `Process` or `ProcessAsync` method to transform the target element however you need.
A First Look at the Anchor Tag Helper
The most commonly used built-in tag helper is the Anchor Tag Helper. Instead of hard-coding a URL, you use `asp-controller` and `asp-action` attributes on a standard `<a>` element:

data.text: If you rename a controller or action, every link using the Anchor Tag Helper continues to work without changes. That is the main benefit: your HTML stays correct because it is generated from your route configuration, not from hard-coded strings.
How Tag Helpers Compare to Plain HTML

data.text: Exercise: Add Your First Anchor Tag Helper

data.title: Exercise: Convert hard-coded links to Anchor Tag Helpers
data.description: Replace static anchor tags in an existing view with Anchor Tag Helpers.
steps: Open any MVC project that has a navigation bar or index view with <a> links.
Locate every hard-coded href attribute (for example, href="/Home/Contact").
Replace each one with asp-controller and asp-action attributes.
Run the application and inspect the generated HTML in the browser DevTools to confirm the href is correct.
Try changing a controller name in the code and verify the link still works.
data.expectedOutcome: All navigation links are generated by the Anchor Tag Helper and remain correct even if routes change.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tag Helpers transform HTML elements at render time using C# code.
Register built-in tag helpers once in _ViewImports.cshtml.
The Anchor Tag Helper replaces hard-coded href values with route-aware attributes.
Custom tag helpers let you encapsulate reusable HTML transformations in C# classes.
data.takeaway: You now know what tag helpers are and why they matter. Next you will explore every major built-in tag helper before writing your own.
